factors. as unit 1 approached this other vehicle from behind, unit 1 failed to control speed and in order to avoid impact with this vehicle, unit 1 took faulty evasive action by swerving to the right, also into the private parking lot of [roadway] 281 s. unit 2 was parked in the front parking lot of [roadway] 281 and into the parking lot, unit 1 continued until the front of unit 1 impacted the rear right of unit 2. during this time the six (6) listed pedestrians were standing in the parking lot between their vehicle and unit 2. the force from the impact caused unit 2 to shift vehemently into the pedestrians causing the pedestrians to be propelled to different areas of the parking lot. unit 2 continued into the front rock wall facade of the structure at [roadway] 281 s, destroying that portion of the structure. debris from the facade fell onto pedestrian listed as unit 3, possibly causing further injury in addition to injuries caused from the vehicles. as a result of the crash there was a total of eight (8) patients needing medical evaluation and treatment including the operator and passenger of unit 1 and six (6) pedestrians, all transported to various hospitals by various means as listed in this report. i briefly spoke with the operator of unit 1 who appeared lucid and cognitive. i had no reason to believe the operator of unit 1 was impaired or intoxicated by drug, alcohol or medical condition other than injuries sustained from the crash. several of the pedestrians provided written statements, consistent with one another that they were congregated in the el charro restaurant parking lot when a blue car (unit 1) entered the parking lot at a high rate of speed before impacting the parked vehicle and the pedestrians. the operator of [roadway] 281 s, slowing to make a turn also provided a written statement indicating she was slowing to make a turn and braced for inevitable impact as she saw unit 1 behind her appear to not be slowing down before swerving to the right towards the parking lot. unit 1 and 2 were both impounded by johnson city towing. while investigating the incident i observed el charro restaurant have several surveillance cameras mounted around the exterior of the building. i requested management to provide video of the incident. on 09/11/[roadway] containing two videos, one interior with a distorted view through the front window [roadway] [roadway] which shows a clear image of the initial [roadway] 281 noticeably at a slower rate [roadway], consistent with slowing to make a legal turn as stated. unit 1 can be seen entering the frame at an [roadway] traffic as also seen in the video. unit 1 is seen swerving into the parking lot in a manner consistent with the stated evasive action. unit 1 continues at approximately this speed until the view of unit 1 is blocked by a wall before unit 1 rolls backwards, back into view, now damaged, believed by me to be immediately after impact. the locations of patients in the diagram may not be exact but are to the best of my recollection their approximate locations.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit #1 was northeast on us 79n and the driver was ill. the driver of unit #1 said he felt tired and tried to turn left into billy bob's zipline, but came in too fast, and turned when unsafe. unit #1 missed the left turn and bottomed out in the west bar ditch. then unit #1's front left struck unit #2 in the left back quarter, then across the rear of unit #2. unit #2 was a legally parked vehicle at billy bob's, facing west. unit #2 was then pushed into unit #3, a legally parked vehicle, facing west. unit #2's right back quarter struck unit #3 in the left front quarter. unit #1 continued northeast with his front striking the left passenger side of unit #3. unit #1 came to rest upright, facing northeast in the parking area of billy bob's zipline. unit #2 came to rest upright, facing southwest in the parking area. unit #3 came to rest upright, facing west in the parking area. unit #4, a pedestrian that was the owner/driver of unit #3, was standing at unit #3's driver side door during the crash and was knocked to ground. the crash was due to the driver of unit #1 possibly having a diabetic stroke; his blood pressure was extremely high and he advised all he had was a can of fruit punch all day.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was traveling sw on i-30 near the 84mp [roadway]. a pedestrian (unit 2) was running away from another crash he had caused moments before (web crash id: 4117322) and was standing partially in the roadway (pedestrian fail to yield right to vehicle). unit 1 driver stated she saw an object (unit 2) on the edge of the roadway just inside the [roadway] as it made contact with her passenger side mirror. unit 1 driver stated she was unable to avoid a collision, causing right panel damage to unit 1. unit 1 made contact with unit 2's left foot with the front right tire and unit 2's side with the mirror. unit 2 sustained a broken fibula and toe abrasions. unit 1 driver pulled onto the improved shoulder and notified law enforcement at the scene of the first crash complying with tx trc 550. 021. unit 2 continued fleeing the scene, and was located approximately . 5 miles ne of the crash scene, holding part of the mirror from unit 1. the pedestrian (unit 2) was impaired due to drugs and alcohol, and arrested for driving while intoxicated. unit 2 refused to provide a specimen of his breath or blood. a blood search warrant was obtained and executed, and the blood specimen was submitted to the dps crime lab in tyler tx for alcohol and drug concentration analysis. ***supplement: blood analysis received from dps crime lab tyler on october 18, 2022, shows 0. 043 bac, blood draw was performed 2 hours and 52 minutes after crash. still awaiting drug analysis****

records.deidentified_narrative: 956 [roadway] residential roadway with no median (traffic east and westbound). 900 kings [roadway] residential roadway with no median (traffic north and southbound). in addition, 900 kings river t-intersects with 900 abe goldberg. unit #1 advised he was traveling eastbound on abe goldberg approximately 15 miles per hour as he was traveling slow due to the fact he was looking for an address (home he was going to exterminate). as he was approaching 956 abe goldberg, he had to brake quickly as he was able to see the 9 year old pedestrian on her skates. the 9 year old appeared to be traveling fast, from the curvature of the t-intersection, that she rolled on to the rock easement, located at 956 abe goldberg and flew head first onto the front passenger quarter panel of unit 1. the pedestrian stated she was traveling north on kings river with her intent to end up on the driveway of her home located at 956 abe goldberg; however, the velocity her velocity gained from traveling north on kings river's sidewalk with a curve going west on abe goldberg prevented the pedestrian from stopping causing her to run onto rocks on [roadway] causing a collision into the right front of unit #1. unit #1 also stated there was a mobile toilet which obstructed his view which officers confirmed. unit #1 advised he did not see the pedestrian but heard and felt the collision to which he quickly got out of his vehicle and called emergency services. both parties had corroborating stories of the incident. the pedestrian was transported by rescue #[medical facility] (umc) due to her head trauma and injuries in general. the officers observed the pedestrian to have visible injuries on her forehead, face, knees, elbows and right hand area. the injury on the forehead was a quarter size bump with scrapes to the face. further injuries to the elbow, knees and hand were all consistent with scrapes from pedestrian falling onto the gravel. officers conducted a follow up at umc. pedestrian was alert and conscious to tell the story of the incident. medical staff advised of pedestrian's vitals being stable and the vitals did not show that she had any internal injuries. photographs of the injuries were taken and uploaded to the westside regional command photo transfer folder. patrol supervisor sgt. montion 1l43 arrived on scene.

however, the velocity her velocity gained from traveling north on kings river's sidewalk with a curve going west on abe goldberg prevented the pedestrian from stopping causing her to run onto rocks on [roadway] causing a collision into the right front of unit #1. unit #1 also stated there was a mobile toilet which obstructed his view which officers confirmed. unit #1 advised he did not see the pedestrian but heard and felt the collision to which he quickly got out of his vehicle and called emergency services. both parties had corroborating stories of the incident. the pedestrian was transported by rescue #[medical facility] (umc) due to her head trauma and injuries in general. the officers observed the pedestrian to have visible injuries on her forehead, face, knees, elbows and right hand area. the injury on the forehead was a quarter size bump with scrapes to the face. further injuries to the elbow, knees and hand were all consistent with scrapes from pedestrian falling onto the gravel. officers conducted a follow up at umc. pedestrian was alert and conscious to tell the story of the incident. medical staff advised of pedestrian's vitals being stable and the vitals did not show that she had any internal injuries. photographs of the injuries were taken and uploaded to the westside regional command photo transfer folder. patrol supervisor sgt. montion 1l43 arrived on scene.

appearing to be in major pain. officer phillips was then able to observe surveillance footage while at walmart. at 1801 hours, otis is seen near the cart return bay as he clocks out. otis is later seen walking across the parking lot while the maroon suv is attempting to leave the parking lot. as the suv enters the crosswalk, otis is seen slamming his hands onto the front hood as the suv simultaneously slammed on its brakes. in officer phillips' opinion, it did not look like the vehicle ever made contact with otis as he is later seen walking off perfectly fine. officer phillips notes that after otis walked off, the suv stayed for a couple of seconds and left as otis continued to walk off. as the suv left the scene, otis is then seen bending over at his hips with his hands over both knees as if he was frustrated. while looking at a different angled camera, officer phillips was able to observed a maroon gmc yukon bearing txlp [identifier] leaving the [roadway]. a short while later, officer phillips received a vehicle return for the yukon which showed alison strickland as the registered owner. dispatch was able to provide a phone number for alison and officer phillips attempted to contact her. alison answered the phone and officer phillips advised her of why she was being contacted. when asked, alison stated that the above referenced txlp for the yukon belonged to her and she confirmed she was at walmart on this date. alison advised that she did in [roadway] at walmart involving the victim and [roadway]. alison stated that while attempting to leave the parking lot, a vehicle displaying a handicap placard turned into the crosswalk before she did which caused her to have to make a wider turn. alison stated as she then slowly merged into the crosswalk, she observed the victim in between her vehicle and the vehicle with the handicap placard and slammed on her brakes. as alison came to a complete stop, she said the victim slammed his hands onto her hood and yelled at her and said ""you almost hit me, [roadway] lady"". alison stated she apologized to the victim and asked if she hit him to which he stated no then proceeded to walk away. alison said she stayed a short while to see if the victim wanted to speak further to her but he continued walking away so she left. alison was provided with officer phillips' email address where she would later send a statement.

u2 appeared to be having trouble breathing, so he was placed in the recovery position as myself and ofc. garcia 278 performed a march assessment of u2. i observed u2 to have a large cut to the back side of his head. i placed a compression bandage on u2's head and held pressure until fire/ems arrived to tend to u2's medical needs. u2 was wearing a dark navy jacket and black pants at the time of the accident. at this time i spoke with u1. u1 was apologetic and she was cooperative throughout the course of the call. u1 stated to me she was driving [roadway] #2 and she did not observe anything in the roadway. u1 stated that she was cruising along at approximately 35mph when all of a sudden she hit something in the roadway. u1 stated she immediately pulled over because she believed she had hit a dog. u1 stated she exited her vehicle and witnessed u2 to be lying on the ground in the center of the roadway. u1 stated again that she did not see u2 at all [roadway]. throughout my interview with u1 i did not observe any indicators that would lead me to believe she was under the influence of any intoxicant. u2 did not cross the roadway at any marked pedestrian crosswalk, and it appears u2 was crossing the roadway in a dimly lit area wearing dark clothing. ofc. evans 271 stood by with u1 as i went to notify tid about the crash. i notified tid and was informed they would be making the incident location to perform their investigation. no witnesses stuck around at the incident location to provide a statement [medical facility] due to his life threatening condition on scene. csi m. guerra 9440 arrived to the scene and photographed the crash location as well as involved parties. tid arrived and received update that u2 was considered to be stable. tid performed interview on scene and determined we no longer needed to hold the location. u1 was provided a [case id] for her documentation. u2's property was collected and placed in the sapd property room by ofc. garcia 278 for records.public_safe_text: unit 1 was [roadway] [roadway], [roadway]. unit 2, a pedestrian, was walking northbound in the crosswalk, [roadway]. unit 2 failed to yield right of way to unit 1, by crossing the roadway, while unit 1 had a green light. unit 1 collided front concentrated with unit 2 knocking unit 2 to [medical facility] where he was pronounced deceased by medical staff at 9:42pm. witnesses confirmed that unit 1 had a green light and i/o watched the light cycle to confirm unit 2 would never have had a signal to cross while unit 1 had a green light. dallas county medical examiner's office is using [case id]. the dallas police traffic unit completed a forensic 3d scan of the scene, and a detective from the vehicle crimes unit responded. all video and photos were uploaded to evidence. com under incident number 22-1832234. this is traffic fatality #87 for the city of dallas in 2022. see related [case id]. this report is incomplete pending toxicology results for unit 2. this report is being supplemented on [date] to include the blood alcohol for unit 2 to be negative for alcohol and positive for the following drugs: cocaine: 32. 3 +/-5. 5 ng/ml, ecgonine methyl ester: 168. 0 +/-25. 2 ng/ml, benzoylecgonine: 1370. 6 +/-301. 5 ng/ml, carboxytetrahydrocannabinol: 2. 7 +/-0. 4 ng/ml. this report is now complete.
